chapter: Hampton, Andy Kirk and Charlie Barnet
title: Being a Black man in Barnet's band: the Worcester hotel
summary: Barnet does not tolerate prejudice, but the road manager fails to book rooms for McGhee and Holland in Worcester, and Barnet fires him.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: How as it, though, to be a Black man in a White band like that?
Well, it was all right, except that...
I guess there were really no problems with the people i the band.
No, wasn't no problems with the people in the band. Charlie wouldn't go for that shit. If you was prejudiced, you didn't have no business being there, and he let you know that right away.

But there were a few occasions where an incident come up... Like, the road manager wouldn't put my name down on the thing for a reservation for a room or something in White hotels in the... We went to Worcester. Now, you know Worcester is not a real prejudiced place. But he didn't put the names down. So when I went to go check in, I heard someone say, "Well, give him a key for Howard McGhee." And he says, "No, no-no, we don't have no Howard McGhee on here." So I was the only one in the band... No, Peanuts was there, too.

Yeah, we were there. So the guy said, "We don't have no more rooms anyway." So I said, "Oh well..." The next day at rehearsal... Charlie had called a rehearsal for ten o'clock that morning. So the next morning I didn't

show up for rehearsal. So he was mad... Charlie was madder than a wet hen. When I came in the theatre, he said, "Where you been?!" I said, "I was trying to find a place to stay? Why? Did you have a place for me to stay?" So he said, "Oh... What's the matter? Why didn't you stay at the hotel like everybody else?" I said, "Well, I didn't have no reservation there." So... I think Mort was the road manager then. So he said...

I can't think of his last name. Morty, yeah, that's right. Anyway, Charlie said, "Get him. Tell him I said come here." So I said, "You tell him. I ain't gonna tell him nothin'." I said, "He don't like me; at least he didn't get no room." I said, "I had to walk all night damn near before I found a place to sleep." So when I went to sleep I wasn't thinking about getting up to make no ten o'clock rehearsal."

So he fired him right on the spot. He said, "How come you didn't have the rooms reserved for Holland and McGhee." He said, "You didn't tell me to make them reservations." So Charlie said, "Well, they're in the band, ain't they, fool?" Oh boy, it was something else, man.
But you know, you'd run into some instances like that. A couple of times you'd run into some situations where...
